records.reason: m125 at 1/1, 150 uL sample and 300 uL DCM begins a four-point ratio/loading-volume experiment. At 100 uL sample, measured endpoints differed substantially between 300 and 500 uL DCM, while current predictions barely distinguish those loading volumes.

The matched m125 1/1, 150 uL sample, 500 uL DCM point isolates loading-volume response within this batch. It tests whether the later finish measured with 500 uL DCM at 100 uL sample recurs at a second sample amount.

m125 at 2/1, 150 uL sample and 300 uL DCM extends the factorial contrast to a weaker mobile phase. The measured 100 uL sample references show different endpoint shapes between loading volumes, making this a useful interaction test.
The m125 2/1, 150 uL sample, 500 uL DCM point completes the quartet. At 100 uL sample, 500 uL DCM gave earlier onset but much later completion than 300 uL DCM; this tests whether that pattern recurs.

m101 at 5/1 and approximately 100 mg fills the loading gap between measured approximately 50 mg behavior at 6.47/13.62 mL and approximately 150 mg behavior at 28.58/28.64 mL. It discriminates a sharp loading response from interpolation toward an unusual record.

This eligible m101 row matches the recorded conditions of the unusual approximately 150 mg measurement. A second label at that tuple tests whether delayed, nearly zero-width elution recurs or reflects variation unresolved by the recorded features, helping interpret the selected intermediate-loading point.
m177 at 1/1 and 150 uL establishes a high-loading baseline below the long finishes measured at 10/1 and 50/1. It helps locate where loading begins to affect V2 independently of onset.

m177 at 5/1 and 100 uL bridges its compact measured 2/1 behavior and longer 10/1 finish. This constrains the lower-ratio tail response and limits inappropriate transfer of the extreme high-loading correction.

m37 at 20/1 and 150 uL completes a loading contrast with measured 50 and 100 uL rows. Their finishes were approximately 97 and 96 mL, whereas this row is predicted to finish near 82 mL. It tests whether loading changes onset more than completion.

m198 at 50/1 and 100 uL extends the ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde curve beyond measured 20/1 behavior. It tests high-ratio transfer within nitro-carbonyl graphs whose onset and finish responses differ substantially by structure and loading.

Para-bromoacetophenone m30 at 50/1 tests transfer of the recent simple-acetophenone failure. Its measured 10/1 reference finished at 23.37 mL; this label establishes the weak-eluent response for a substituted aromatic ketone.

Para-fluoroacetophenone m34 at 50/1 and 50 uL tests the predicted rise to 27.50/52.75 mL beyond measured 20/1 behavior. Together with m30 and measured acetophenone, it probes substituent-dependent transfer across common aryl ketones.

Branched alkyl aryl ketone m54 at 50/1 supplies a predicted compact counterpoint to late acetophenone behavior. Its measured 20/1 row remained compact, so this tests whether carbonyl substitution continues to moderate the weak-eluent response.

m68 at 50/1 tests a predicted transition to 15.99/36.85 mL after measured 10/1 and 20/1 rows retained early onset. This distinguishes a real high-ratio rise from transfer driven by other aromatic ketones.

Methoxy-substituted ethyl benzoate m87 at 50/1 extends measured 20/1 behavior of approximately 12.01/27.92 mL. The predicted 26.92/49.02 mL rise tests an uncovered ester response and provides structural context for the paired fluoroester measurements.

m85 at 20/1 and 100 uL begins a matched ratio pair with its selected 50/1 row. Measured 10/1 references anchor the lower-ratio region; this point determines whether the predicted increase develops gradually.

m85 at 50/1 keeps sample amount and loading conditions fixed relative to the selected 20/1 point. Measuring both tests the predicted increase from 12.18/19.61 to 23.10/42.44 mL and teaches a local ester response slope.

Enaminoester m72 at 5/1, 100 uL and PE loading fills the middle of its donor-containing response curve. The measured catalog contains both PE and DCM loading configurations; this label helps constrain their joint relationship with ratio and sample amount.

m72 at 10/1, 50 uL and DCM loading complements measured 150 uL DCM behavior and the measured 5/1, 50 uL DCM point. It supplies a missing loading contrast where long V2 tails make endpoint-specific sensitivity consequential.

m216 at 5/1 and 150 uL extends the newly measured 2/1 high-loading baseline toward its measured 5/1, 100 uL reference. The predicted finish near 50.86 mL tests whether the approximately 57.67 mL finish at 100 uL persists at higher loading.
m141 at 1/1 and 100 uL tests the predicted 8.47/20.29 mL baseline against measured 1/1, 150 uL and 2/1, 100 uL behavior. It constrains the basic-ring tail below the much later PE-rich regime.

Tertiary benzylic alcohol m203 at 20/1 explores a predicted rise to 24.96/41.59 mL beyond measured 10/1 behavior under nearby loading. This extends donor-response learning into a sterically different alcohol environment with compact lower-ratio observations.

m51 at 5/1 and 100 uL fills the gap between measured 2/1 behavior and the late 10/1 regime. It locates the response transition for a tertiary alcohol separated from its aromatic ring by an alkyl chain.

m99 at 5/1 and 50 uL is a missing corner of a ratio-by-loading comparison. Measured references provide 5/1 at 150 uL and 10/1 at 50 uL; this label determines the loading slope before the later regime.

m99 at 10/1 and 150 uL completes the crossed comparison. Its prediction of 34.57/49.59 mL contrasts with measured 44.43/60.99 mL at 50 uL, testing whether loading advances onset, changes completion, or affects both.

m197 at 2/1 and 50 uL tests a predicted V2 dip to 18.47 mL relative to a measured 29.44 mL finish at 1/1 under the same loading conditions. It can reveal either a real nonmonotonic response or a model interpolation failure.

m197 at 10/1 and 100 uL adds an intermediate point below its measured 20/1 and 50/1 rows. Alongside the selected 2/1 point, it tests the predicted depressed-finish region without treating monotonicity as experimental truth.

m120 at 1/1 and 150 uL tests whether its strong loading sensitivity already appears at lower PE fraction. Measured 2/1 rows differ sharply with sample amount, and 5/1 rows show onset changing much more than completion.

Aryl methyl-sulfide ketone m128 at 5/1 and 100 uL forms a loading contrast with measured 50 uL behavior and connects to measured 10/1 high-loading retention. Opposite-signed recent m128 and m129 historical errors favor a graph-specific response over a uniform sulfur-family correction.

Aliphatic chloroketone m27 at 10/1 begins a matched ratio pair in a region lacking measured high-ratio anchors. Its low-ratio observations are compact, whereas this point is predicted at 15.43/25.70 mL. It tests transfer of the learned ketone response.

Aminoester m88 at 2/1 and 100 uL separates ratio response from the loading contrast implicit in measured 1/1, 100 uL and 2/1, 50 uL rows. It improves positional aminoester and endpoint-specific loading calibration.

m27 at 20/1 retains exactly the sample amount and loading conditions of the selected 10/1 point. The pair tests the predicted rise to 21.20/34.31 mL, distinguishing a sustained aliphatic ketone response from unsupported transfer of late retention.

hypotheses.content: Late retention in azaaromatic and nitrile-carbonyl graphs depends strongly on graph and mobile-phase conditions. Recent lower-ratio measurements support localized response curves rather than a global heteroatom-based late correction. Increasing PE/EA generally weakens the normal-phase mobile phase.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Condition-specific labels can refine basic-ring and nitrile-carbonyl response surfaces while protecting comparatively accurate lower-ratio predictions from excessive correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m216 retain its long 5/1 finish at higher loading, and does m141 already have an underrepresented tail at 1/1?

hypotheses.content: Sample loading and graph context can affect V1 and V2 differently. Some families show earlier onset with a nearly unchanged finish, while others develop a much longer finish at higher loading; a universal shift of both endpoints cannot represent these patterns.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading and ratio labels can teach separate onset and completion sensitivities, particularly where predictions vary little across loading or imply an unexplained finish dip.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m177 loading-dependent tails begin, and do the crossed m99 measurements and intermediate-ratio m197 labels support the predicted endpoint shapes?

hypotheses.content: The m125 loading-volume contrasts may represent a reproducible interaction between DCM plug volume and mobile-phase ratio. Current predictions are nearly invariant between 300 and 500 uL DCM despite substantial measured endpoint differences at 100 uL sample; unresolved row variation remains an alternative explanation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The four matched labels test whether loading-solvent volume carries predictive information that the current response surface suppresses. Their joint interpretation can distinguish a condition interaction from inconsistent individual records.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 150 uL sample volume, do 300 versus 500 uL DCM produce reproducible endpoint differences at both 1/1 and 2/1?

hypotheses.content: The m101 5/1 response may contain a sharp loading transition, but its delayed, nearly zero-width high-loading record could instead reflect variation unexplained by the recorded conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An intermediate-loading label plus a second label at the unusual high-loading tuple can distinguish a learnable condition response from unresolved variability and constrain the conditional prediction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the approximately 150 mg tuple again give delayed, narrow elution, and where does the approximately 100 mg label fall relative to the measured endpoints?

hypotheses.content: Ordinary ketones have markedly different weak-eluent responses across carbonyl environments. The recent acetophenone failure shows that useful remaining failure regions extend beyond nitrogen-containing and donor-rich molecules; corrections should depend on structural context.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related ketone labels can discriminate graph-dependent response slopes and reduce inappropriate transfer between late and compact carbonyl environments. The m27 pair explores this relationship outside aromatic carbonyl graphs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do para-halogenated acetophenones and m68 show sustained PE-rich delays while m54 remains compact, and does aliphatic m27 follow its predicted steep response?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes reduce the value of repeatedly repairing already constrained lower-ratio regions. The latest m159 1/1 and 5/1 labels and m211 1/1 and 5/1 labels were comparatively accurate at acquisition. The m216 2/1 labels showed similar finishes across loading, with historical error concentrated more in onset. The latest compact m80 outcome agrees with earlier high-ratio measurements, weakening any broad late-tail correction for that graph. Conversely, the recent m42 50/1 measurement substantially exceeded both acquisition-time predictions, raising the priority of ordinary carbonyl response exploration. Opposite-signed recent m128 and m129 historical errors weaken a uniform sulfur-family correction. The m98 overprediction reinforces the need to constrain ordinary ester behavior alongside extreme tails. I follow observed-table assignments over remembered reasons: the recent record described in memory as intermediate-condition m146 is actually m56 at 20/1. Chemically, 0/1 is pure EA and the strongest listed mobile phase; m128 and m129 are aryl methyl sulfides bearing ketone and aldehyde groups, respectively.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates labels where local experiments can distinguish competing explanations. The m125 quartet tests loading-volume and ratio interactions against predictions that scarcely respond to volume. The m101 pair investigates an apparent loading transition and an unusual interval without presuming that the measured record is erroneous. Crossed m99 additions and m177 baselines target separate onset and completion responses. Paired m85 and m27 ratios provide response slopes in incompletely observed regions, while m197 tests a predicted finish dip. Related ketone, ester, alcohol, aminoester, and azaaromatic points connect measured failures to other structures and ordinary-row behavior. Predicted compact m54 behavior and lower-ratio donor points constrain how far late-retention corrections should transfer. These labels may improve overall Row-distribution accuracy by teaching graph-condition interactions and endpoint-specific sensitivities while limiting redundancy in already accurate curves. Retraining benefit remains untested, and variation unexplained by recorded variables may persist. All 32 IDs and their supplied predictions are fixed before any new label reveal.
